process.title: Discovery
process.description: We understand the business goal, the audience, the brand constraints, and the technical limits. I define scope, risks, and deliverables before choosing tools or writing a line of code.

process.title: Design, systems & architecture
process.description: I define the architecture, the content model, and the design system: tokens, components, and patterns. I prototype key screens and flows (web, CMS, and automation/AI touchpoints) to validate direction before building at scale.

process.title: Build & automation
process.description: I build in short iterations with verifiable deliveries: typed, accessible, and optimized implementations across web frameworks, CMS, and workflows (n8n, MCP, and more), deployed to previews from day one.

process.title: Delivery, handoff & ownership
process.description: Deploy to production, set up analytics and automation, and create living documentation and training so your team can keep iterating and own the system without depending on me for every change.

faq.q: How is a project measured in Essentials and Growth?
faq.a: A base project is a complete site of up to four sections (for example, a home plus 3 sections), with a maximum of 6 strips per page so a single page doesn't grow without limit. It's the unit I use to measure monthly capacity. When scope grows, it's normalized: an eight-section site counts as two base projects, even if it's a single URL, because the work equals two. Pieces with their own logic, like an online store (catalog, cart, checkout), aren't a base project; they're quoted separately or as several units depending on scope. That way "5 projects per month" means clear, measurable capacity, not an ambiguous number. Visionary, by contrast, is measured by hours of dedicated engineering, not by projects, given the variable scope of its initiatives.

faq.q: What does the Visionary package include?
a: Visionary is the technical partner tier. It includes everything in Growth and adds architecture for content platforms, editorial sites, and complex web systems; implementation in modern frameworks like Next.js, Astro, and Payload; and advanced automations, assistants, chatbots, and AI flows connected to your real operation.

It gives you the technical foundation to open premium offerings like online stores, content platforms, and brand experiences powered by AI, the capacity that usually requires an in-house technical team without having to build one. It's measured by 36 hours of dedicated engineering per month, plus a weekly studio visit and advisory meetings as extra time.

faq.q: How do meetings and studio visits work?
faq.a: Meetings and the weekly studio visit are extra time included: they don't consume your projects or Visionary's hours. Growth includes up to 4 hours of meetings per week and Visionary up to 8, plus a weekly studio visit for alignment and in-person planning. Essentials focuses on implementation, with no recurring meetings included. The intent is that strategy and alignment don't cost you delivery capacity.

faq.q: What does each retainer's scope cover?
faq.a: Each retainer is based on a capacity defined up front: base projects on Essentials and Growth, or hours on Visionary, across agreed types of work (sites, landings, CMS, automations, etc.). Any initiative outside that capacity is quoted as an additional project. It isn't «whatever comes up that month», but a fixed web engineering and design capacity used against a backlog agreed with Pigmento.

faq.q: How is a project priced?
faq.a: I start from the discovery scope. For scoped pieces I use a fixed price; for full projects I quote by scope; and for ongoing work I use a monthly retainer.

faq.q: How is the backlog prioritized?
faq.a: Requests are grouped into a monthly backlog. We prioritize together with Pigmento what goes into each cycle; whatever doesn't fit moves to the next one, or is quoted as a separate project if it needs extra urgency.

faq.q: How are responsibilities shared?
faq.a: Pigmento keeps control over brand strategy, content, and the relationship with its clients; I own the web layer, systems, and automations within the defined scope. Any major strategic change is reviewed before taking it on within the retainer.

faq.q: Are tools and licenses included?
faq.a: Use of my toolbox (Figma, Adobe, motion libs, CMS, n8n, Claude, Cursor, etc.) is included in the retainer. Specific enterprise licenses, third-party infrastructure, or accounts owned by the client are budgeted separately when needed.

faq.q: What about infrastructure and major support?
faq.a: Packages cover design, implementation, automations, and standard deploys. Major infrastructure changes (hosting migrations, full stack refactors, adopting new platforms) are framed as projects with their own scope.

faq.q: Can you join an existing team?
faq.a: Yes. I plug into your processes, repos, and tools, or I lead the web technical side end to end, whatever you need.

faq.q: What stack do you use?
a: I work with modern JS frameworks like Next.js, Astro, and React, with TypeScript and token-based design systems for UI.
For content and data I use CMSs and APIs such as Payload, Strapi, Webflow, and headless WordPress, plus workflow automation with n8n when it helps the team.
Infrastructure usually runs on Vercel and Cloudflare, with Supabase/Postgres and CI/CD where the project needs it.
On top of that, I integrate AI tooling (Claude, MCP servers, agents) to support documentation, content, and internal workflows when it adds real value.
The stack is always adapted to the project and to how much ownership your team wants over the final system, not to a single “favorite tool”.

faq.q: Do you work remotely?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with teams in North America, LATAM, and Europe, in time zones compatible with the Americas.

faq.q: Can you include these projects in your portfolio?
faq.a: Yes, but only as attribution, never as ownership. If I feature any of the projects I build for Pigmento Studio, I always present it as a collaboration: I credit my role in building it, without claiming the project as my own.

proposalsMoeasy.hero_subtitle: I handle the technical side of your projects and stay behind: the face, the brand and the client relationship are yours. Here's everything on MoEasy, what I found, what I propose, what it costs and what you can sell around it. And any technical question that comes up in the meeting, I answer it before you need it.
proposalsMoeasy.situacion_sub: Everything below comes from reviewing their current site, not from assumptions. Every point can be verified at moeasy.com.mx.
proposalsMoeasy.complicacion_sub: We reviewed moeasy.com.mx before writing this proposal. This is what we found, ordered by what it costs. Every point can be verified by visiting the site.

problems.title: The listing page captures no leads at all
problems.body: The only forms on a listing are the currency selector, the language selector and search. There's no contact form, no email, no phone, no WhatsApp. All a prospect can do from a property is share it.
problems.cost: Anyone interested has to leave the property, find the contact page and start from scratch. Real estate sites convert visitors to leads at around 1% to 3%; with no capture on the listing, that conversion happens off the site or not at all.

problems.title: The listing doesn't carry the numbers that close a deal
problems.body: One template for house, warehouse, office and retail unit. There's no clear height, loading docks, electrical capacity or zoning.
problems.cost: 80% of tenants and 78% of investors in commercial real estate say the internet is essential to their search. For that segment the listing isn't advertising, it's the qualification process. If the number isn't there, the team ends up qualifying over WhatsApp what the page should have answered on its own.

problems.title: Nobody can search the way they buy
problems.body: Eight separate collections mix operation, segment and subtype. There's no way to combine lease, office, area and budget in a single view.
problems.cost: Every missing filter is a longer list to scan by hand. The search ends on a portal, where MoEasy sits next to every competitor and the conversation starts with price.

problems.title: The lead that does arrive carries no property and no owner
problems.body: Contact is generic and doesn't travel with the property that produced it, so nobody knows which asset is being discussed or whose job it is to answer.
problems.cost: Answering within five minutes makes qualifying a lead 21 times more likely than answering in thirty. In a study of 74 brokerages, 41% never answered a web inquiry at all. With no property and no owner, there's no clock to start.

proposalsMoeasy.tiers_heading: Three routes, and the difference is where the inventory lives.
proposalsMoeasy.tiers_subtitle: MoEasy isn't starting from zero: it already runs its inventory from its own CRM, hosted on a server in China, with its own operating logic. The first two packages connect to none of that and build a site from scratch. The third sits on top of what they already have. That's the real decision, and it's what explains the price difference.

tiers.label: To launch fast
tiers.name: Express catalog
tiers.tagline: Gets MoEasy out of store logic in three weeks, with their own team in charge and no dependency on anyone to publish.
tiers.rationale: It's the lowest-risk route and the fastest to approve. It fixes what's visible from the first click: an investor looking for a 2,000 m2 industrial warehouse lands on a page talking about carts, favorites and sale prices. What it doesn't fix is the internal operation, which is why it's the cheapest package, not the most convenient one.

To size the return: with industrial rent in Mexico City at 10.32 USD per m2 per month, the commission on a single 2,000 m2 lease is around 20,000 USD. One additional deal a year covers the whole project with room to spare.

proposalsMoeasy.alternatives_sub: MoEasy will find these options if they look, and all of them are cheaper than building. Better that Pigmento knows them before the client does, with the answer already in hand.

alternatives_rows.name: Real estate CRM with a site included
alternatives_rows.cost: $1,490 per month for 50 listings, plus $500 per month for the site. Around $24,000 a year.
alternatives_rows.why: It would be the right option if MoEasy only sold houses, and it's worth saying so plainly. But the site comes from nine templates, so it looks like every other brokerage in the country, and its data model is residential: no clear height, no loading docks, no zoning. It's also rent. The day they stop paying, the site is gone.

alternatives_rows.name: WordPress with a real estate theme
alternatives_rows.cost: A license of around $79 USD once, plus the development.
alternatives_rows.why: Technically this is the closest alternative: it ships with a CRM, advanced search and custom fields for commercial properties. The real cost isn't the license, it's maintenance. A real estate theme lives on plugins, and when hosting updates the PHP version things break silently: notifications that stop going out, forms that never arrive, inventories out of sync. That gets paid in lost deals, not in license fees.

alternatives_rows.name: Publishing only on portals
alternatives_rows.cost: Professional plans from $1,899 per month for five listings. The featured version, $5,742 per month for five.
alternatives_rows.why: With inventory in the dozens the number climbs fast, and it's rented traffic. Each MoEasy listing competes against the one beside it on the same page, with no brand and no control of the context. It works as an acquisition channel, not as a home.

alternatives_rows.name: Redesigning the current Shopify theme
alternatives_rows.cost: The cheapest of all the options.
alternatives_rows.why: It changes how it looks, not what it models. Listings stay products with a cart, a sale price and store URLs. The problem isn't aesthetic.

alternatives_rows.name: Building it custom
alternatives_rows.cost: $45,000 to $155,000 once, depending on the package.
alternatives_rows.why: It's the only one that holds up the commercial half of the business, which is exactly what separates MoEasy from a residential brokerage. In its full version it sits on the infrastructure they already run, instead of opening a parallel system. Paid once, and the asset stays theirs.

proposalsMoeasy.choose_note: The connected platform is the recommendation, and the argument isn't that it's more modern. MoEasy already captures its inventory in its own system: any route that doesn't read from it is asking them to do the same work twice, every day, forever.
proposalsMoeasy.objections_heading: Never lower the rate without lowering the scope.
proposalsMoeasy.objections_sub: Every objection has an answer and a safe concession. The concession cuts scope, not the price for the same work.

objections_rows.response: We can keep the main outcome and reduce operational complexity, not the quality of what gets delivered.
objections_rows.concession: Move to the express package, reduce the number of migrated properties, leave the extra language as phase two.

objections_rows.objection: We want all of it, just cheaper
objections_rows.response: The responsible way to lower the investment is to prioritize a first phase, not to remove the invisible hours of architecture, QA and launch, which are the ones that keep the site from failing in production.
objections_rows.concession: Home, catalog, listing page and lead capture now. Services and about in a second delivery.

objections_rows.response: Confirmed in discovery: the audience is Chinese clients living in Mexico and the site is administered from their offices, so there's no connectivity risk. All three languages fit in Webflow's localization plan at nine dollars a month, and they're native in the connected platform. What is separate work is the translated copy and who answers in that language.
objections_rows.concession: Multilingual infrastructure included in all three routes, Mandarin content as an add-on.

objections_rows.objection: We want maps and a CRM too
objections_rows.response: They're valuable extensions and we'll want them. They affect the data model, routing and testing, so they're quoted as a later phase with their own scope.
objections_rows.concession: Leave the integration points designed, without building them.

objections_rows.objection: Why not keep it on Shopify?
objections_rows.response: Shopify will keep being excellent for commerce. This project solves something else: asset exploration, qualification and real estate contact. It isn't a judgment about the tool, it's that its core object is the product and the cart.
objections_rows.concession: If speed is what rules, move to the express package and evolve later.

objections_rows.objection: A real estate CRM costs us two thousand a month
objections_rows.response: And it would be the right option if you were starting from zero. You already have a CRM with your inventory inside it. What's missing isn't another system to capture in, it's the site reading from the one you already use. On top of that, its site comes from nine templates and its data model is residential: no clear height, no loading docks, no zoning.
objections_rows.concession: If the commercial inventory were marginal, recommend it honestly and quote only the brand work.

proposalsMoeasy.why_heading: Why we sell this, and why Pigmento sells it.
proposalsMoeasy.why_sub: A redesign is justified with taste. A platform is justified with business. This is the logic behind what's being proposed, so it can be defended in a meeting without talking about technology.
proposalsMoeasy.why_product_label: Why this and not a redesign

why_product.title: The problem isn't how it looks
why_product.body: The audit didn't find an ugly site. It found a site that captures no leads, doesn't provide the numbers that qualify a commercial deal, and forces the inventory to be captured twice. None of that gets fixed with design.

why_product.title: The commercial inventory is what pays
why_product.body: Four lines of business, and the one with the highest ticket and longest cycle is the worst served by the current site. That's where the return is, and that's where the proposal concentrates.

why_product.title: The source of truth already exists
why_product.body: MoEasy already runs its inventory from its own CRM, hosted on a server in China, with the operating logic their team built. Standing up a site in parallel asks them to maintain two systems forever. Reading from the one they have respects what works and publishes it well. That difference is what separates the three routes.

why_product.title: The market already works this way
why_product.body: Their direct competition filters across criteria, publishes commercial specs and captures from the listing. This doesn't get sold as innovation, it gets sold as parity.

why_pigmento.title: The relationship is yours
why_pigmento.body: MoEasy trusts Pigmento because of the brand work. Development comes in through that door, not the other way around. Nobody gets to that conversation before you.

why_pigmento.title: The technical risk isn't yours
why_pigmento.body: Scope, architecture, integration and warranty are on me. You answer to the client for the result, not for the code.

why_pigmento.title: It opens an account, it doesn't close a project
why_pigmento.body: Maintenance, new listings, content, campaigns and CRM are services Pigmento bills later, with the technical backing already in place.

why_pigmento.title: The price leaves real margin
why_pigmento.body: What the market charges for a project like this sits above what it costs here. That difference is yours, and it's documented in the previous section.

solutions.title: Every property becomes a point of contact
solutions.body: Every listing carries its own information request form. The message arrives with the property, the area and the assigned advisor already inside, so nobody has to ask which asset it's about or whose turn it is.
solutions.forecast: Real estate sites convert between 1% and 3% of visitors into contacts. Today that conversion can't happen on the listing, so the first effect isn't a better percentage: it's that the percentage starts to exist. And because the lead arrives identified, it can be answered in minutes. Answering within five makes qualifying it 21 times more likely than answering in thirty.
solutions.source: MIT with InsideSales, across 1.25 million leads

solutions.title: A search that leads to choosing, not to browsing
solutions.body: Operation, property type, area, budget and floor space combine on the same screen. Someone looking for a warehouse in a given corridor under a given price reaches their shortlist in one step, not by walking through eight sections.
solutions.forecast: 43% of visitors go straight to the search bar, and searchers convert at 4.63% against 2.77% for browsers: nearly double. Airbnb built its growth on this idea and published the research, measured with A/B tests: recommending the right filters moves bookings, not just clicks.
solutions.source: Econsultancy and Airbnb's search filter research

solutions.title: The listing adapts to the asset, the way Airbnb does
solutions.body: A house shows bedrooms and bathrooms. A warehouse shows clear height, loading docks, electrical capacity and zoning. The visitor sees only what they need to decide, and the team captures only what applies to that asset.
solutions.forecast: It's the same mechanism Airbnb uses: choosing an entire home surfaces kitchen and workspace; choosing a private room surfaces shared spaces. With 80% of commercial tenants qualifying online before contacting an advisor, the listing stops being advertising and becomes the tool that decides whether there's a visit.

solutions.title: One place to administer, and permissions to delegate
solutions.body: The team publishes, edits and removes from a single screen, with the fields that belong to each property type and without touching code. Permissions are split by role, so the workload can be delegated without opening the whole site to everyone.
solutions.forecast: On the connected platform, nobody captures twice either: the site reads from the system Marketing already works in. Every property re-entered by hand is team time that doesn't come back, and every value updated on only one side is a listing published wrong.

tiers_common: Custom design on MoEasy's identity, responsive from mobile to desktop.
Information request form on every listing, with the property and the advisor already identified in the message.
WhatsApp contact from every property, which is where deals actually close in Mexico.
Every listing ready to share: sending the link over WhatsApp shows the property, not a generic logo.
On-page SEO and GEO for search engines and AI engines, across the inventory and not only the static pages.
Infrastructure setup: deployment, connected domain and security certificate.
Baseline analytics with contact events, to know which properties generate messages.
Team training and fifteen days of warranty after going live.
